label: “Graft these CDRs onto a stable human framework.”
prompt: Graft these CDRs onto a stable human framework. (protein design)
answerHead:
BioMate

Antibody Antigen Complex — Co-folds an antibody and antigen structure from sequences, predicting the bound complex geometry and interface interactions.

Input: Demo antibody–antigen pair (FMC63 scFv × CD19 fragment); the workflow does not read your attached PDB/FASTA files
Key steps:
Boltz-2 / AlphaFold3 multi-chain co-folding → predicted complex structure (PDB)
Interface analysis → contact map, buried surface area, interaction energies
CDR orientation and pairing geometry scoring
Expected output: Complex structure (PDB), interface contact table, interaction summary, confidence metrics (pAE, pLDDT per chain)

To graft your nanobody CDRs onto the human b12 framework and validate the design, this workflow runs co-folding on the default demo pair. To use your sequences (H11-D4 CDRs + 1HZH b12 framework), you have two options:

Paste your antibody and antigen sequences directly into the workflow parameters as JSON — the panel accepts a JSON-formatted antibody_chains and antigen_chains input instead of the defaults. This lets you keep all your CDR grafting logic and constraints in the JSON spec.

Use a dedicated CDR grafting + design workflow — search for scfv_antibody_design or antibody_developability (these read PDB + FASTA directly and handle framework/CDR boundary annotation, constraint parsing, and expression/stability prediction). Which would you prefer?

Antibody Antigen Complex
